newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cabinet approves $1.47 billion power plant.
newsitem.headline: Indian cabinet approves $1.47 billion power plant.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Friday approved a proposal by Central India Power Co Ltd to set up a $1.47 billion power plant in the western state of Maharashtra, the government said in a statement.

The 1,082-megawatt plant would have $444 million in foreign equity held jointly by a consortium led by Denro Ispat Ltd, as well as by GEC Alsthom Ltd, Electricite de France (EDF) and their affiliates, it said.
The consortium led by Denro Ispat would hold 53 percent of the $444 million foreign stake.

GEC-Alsthom, a joint venture between Britain's General Electric Co Plc and France's Alcatel Alsthom, and its affiliates would hold 31.8 percent of the foreign stake. EDF and its partners would own 15.2 percent.
The $444 million foreign stake marked an increase over an earlier proposed $270 million foreign holding, the statement said.
While the foreign equity in the joint venture has been raised, the capital cost has been scaled down to $1.47 billion from $1.64 billion.
